nodes.question: In the edited image, can the source-image paper and cup be identified, and is that paper visibly stuffed inside that cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if the edited image provides enough visual evidence to identify the same paper and cup shown in the source and shows the paper placed inside the cup with evidence it has been stuffed into it. Fail only if both objects are identifiable and the paper is visibly outside the cup or merely on its rim. Unknown if either object's identity, or their placement, cannot be established.
nodes.binding: Anchor “the paper” and “the cup” to the objects in the source image. Do not treat a visually different-looking item or object in the edited image as the same object without sufficient evidence.

Fail only if both objects are identifiable and there is visibly no progress toward the requested placement, or s1 establishes completion. Unknown if either object's identity or the relevant progress relation cannot be established.
nodes.binding: Progress counts only when it advances stuffing the source-image paper into the source-image cup. Do not infer absence of progress from uncertain object identity or proximity.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. You receive no reference label or optimization feedback. Return status, evidence, reported confidence (0..1 or null), and used_dependency_ids naming every supplied context check_id exactly once in saved order.
Supports receive source and edited images. Answer only the saved proposition using its binding and criteria. Use pass/fail/unknown. Context is advisory unless listed in required_dependencies. A negative context observation is usable evidence. Unknown, skipped, or invalid context is not a failure and must not stop an independent image inspection. Inspect the images yourself; do not repeat a parent's answer. Return unknown when the relevant fact cannot be established. Confidence reports confidence in this answer, not calibrated correctness.
Fulfillment receives NO images. Use only saved support evidence, original instruction/rubric and frozen composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Supporting passes answer specific propositions, not a count of completed edits. Their polarity can differ. Apply saved alternatives: optional uncertainty need not prevent a known outcome, but a required unresolved fact makes that outcome unresolved. Never invent a visual fact or convert missing evidence into failure. A conditional skip is not non-applicability. All applicable requested outcomes complete gives yes; no requested progress gives no; known progress short of completion gives partial. Unrelated changes are not progress.

fulfillment: The node’s binding already captures the requested end state and distinguishes stuffing from merely being near/on the rim; do not relax that criterion. The unresolved result appears driven by identity/evidence handling: the source visibly has a white sheet and blue cup, while the edit shows a hand-held blue printed sheet and a reddish rounded object. These do not visibly establish either the same paper/cup or any progress toward stuffing, so the reference “no” is consistent with the rubric, but is not atomic ground truth. Improve the node’s evidence routing so completion and progress are assessed separately against the source and instruction: count only visually supported changes to the requested paper/cup action, and treat unrelated or unidentifiable objects as no demonstrated progress when the images support that conclusion; retain unknown when identity or progress genuinely cannot be resolved. Avoid turning high confidence in an unresolved trace into a forced label. There is no transport, schema, or dependency failure indicated: both supports were queried and valid, and the aggregate is unresolved because their visual evidence did not resolve the decision.
s2: The current binding is too restrictive for the rubric: it makes uncertain identity or proximity block a no-progress judgment, so this trace stays unresolved even though the edit shows a hand-held printed item beside a reddish object, with no visible placement into or movement toward the source paper and blue cup. Refine the decision criteria to assess observable progress separately from object identity: compare source and edit, and when the edit provides no visual evidence of the requested paper-to-cup action, allow a no-progress result; reserve unknown for cases where the images leave plausible requested progress genuinely unresolved. Do not treat the reference label as proof, and do not infer that the objects are unrelated solely from their changed appearance. Keep completion distinct from partial progress, and do not relax the requirement that progress must advance stuffing the paper into the cup. The trace is valid and queried, with no transport, schema, or dependency failure; the issue is semantic evidence routing, not execution.
s1: The binding anchors the objects but the node’s criteria conflate completion with whether the source objects can be identified: they permit “fail” only after both identities are established and the paper is visibly outside/on the rim. That leaves no-progress edits unresolved when the edit instead shows no observable paper-to-cup action. Preserve the source-object anchor and the stuffing requirement, but route the decision through the rubric’s separate outcomes: assess completion, then any visually supported partial progress toward stuffing, and use “no” only when the images support that no requested change has progressed; reserve unknown for genuine ambiguity about whether progress occurred. Here the edit shows a hand-held printed item and a reddish object, with no visible stuffing or movement toward it. Do not infer identity from appearance alone, but do not let uncertain identity automatically block a no-progress judgment. Keep unrelated edits distinct from requested progress, and do not use the reference label as proof. The trace is valid and queried; this is semantic criterion/routing ambiguity, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure.
